proof_summary: Modulo 2, Lucas’s theorem characterizes a contributing triple \((n,k,j)\), with \(m=n(k+1)+j(n+1)\), by the bit conditions \(k\mathbin{\&}n=k\) and \(n\mathbin{\&}j=0\). The involution sending it to the triple whose first two coordinates are \((k+j,\,n\mathbin{\&}(k+j))\) preserves the contribution and pairs all terms except fixed points, which force \(k=n\) and \(j=0\), hence \(m=n(n+1)\).
